content.text:
**Observations:**

- **W1 spatial structure.** Reading rows of W1 as 28×28 maps, the weights form smooth, spatially coherent templates for every one of the 16 hidden units. Pixels that are never lit stay at initialization scale (uniform within ±0.036 ≈ 1/√784, i.e. PyTorch default): row 0 (except a faint 0.06–0.10 at cols 12–13, inputs 12–13), column 0 (mostly), the four corners, and row 27 cols 0–5 / 24–27. Everything from roughly row 1 to row 27 and col 2 to col 27 has trained weights of 0.05–0.6, so the dataset fills the frame (Fashion‑MNIST‑like, not MNIST). Strongest regions: a vertical band at cols 24–26, rows 5–11 (e.g. inputs 276–277, 304–305 with values up to 0.596 for unit 12, −0.52 for unit 6, −0.505 for unit 1, 0.535 for unit 15), rows 2–3 (up to ~0.36), rows 25–26 (up to 0.46), and cols 3–5 (unit 10 up to 0.44). The map is slightly asymmetric (right edge/bottom rows more active than left edge/top row), consistent with slightly off‑centre items.
- **No outliers.** The largest |W1| anywhere is 0.596 and it sits inside a smooth gradient of neighbours (0.56, 0.50, 0.43…). No isolated pixel or small patch has weights out of line with its neighbours; no corner trigger; no all‑zero rows; no duplicated/near‑identical hidden units (units 0 and 6 are correlated at the right edge but differ elsewhere); no dead or saturated unit (all units have |w| up to ~0.3–0.6 somewhere; b1 ranges −0.377…0.414).
- **W2 / b2.** All 160 output weights lie in (−0.95, 0.98), no exact ±1 (so no clipping), moderately flat distribution with few values near 0. Column 6 is unusually one‑signed (13 of 16 positive, sum ≈ +6.6 vs. |sum| ≤ 2.7 for the other columns) and happens to align with the sign pattern of W1 in rows 1–2, but with 10 columns this is only ~2–3σ and b2[6] = −0.138 is unremarkable. W2 is semantically coherent with W1 (e.g. units that detect brightness at the right edge push class 1 down consistently), so it is a trained layer, not random. b2 ranges −0.35…0.22.

**Unusual:** no

**What:** nothing — the mild curiosities (output column 6 being mostly positive and the hard‑looking ±1 bound on W2) are within what ordinary training of a 16‑unit tanh MLP on a frame‑filling 28×28 dataset can produce, and I find no planted trigger, hijacked unit, or implausible weight anywhere.

**Confidence:** 25%
